newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 2 to 851 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 2 to 851 in latest week.

text.p: There were at 851 rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States as of Nov. 22, up two from the prior week and 72 above the year-ago total of 774, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by one to 717, while rigs working offshore dipped one to 107. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by two to 27.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in New Mexico, which showed an increase of five and California, which showed a decrease of four. Louisiana rose by three.

A total of 374 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up eight from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by six to 475, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
There were 189 rigs drilling directionally, 65 drilling horizontally and 597 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 18 to 341 vs. 216 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 164 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Nov. 22, down one from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was 91.6 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean remained the same this week at 106 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count remained unchanged at 564 out of a total fleet of 604, making the utilization rate 93.4 percent.
